name: How Can I Keep a Kitchen Renovation Dust-Free in an Occupied San Diego Home?

mainEntity.name: What dust and access controls should a contractor provide when I live in the house during a kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: What dust and access controls should a contractor provide when I live in the house during a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Living at home during a kitchen renovation requires a written protection plan, not just a promise to clean up. Ask how the crew will separate the work zone, protect flooring, cover furniture, control airborne dust, store tools, remove debris, and keep doors secured. Clarify whether HVAC returns will be protected and how workers will prevent dust from spreading through the home. Set rules for pets, children, visitors, deliveries, alarms, locked doors, and access to bathrooms or utility rooms. Establish a temporary kitchen with safe electrical service, refrigerator access, water, lighting, and food storage. Ask who disconnects and reconnects appliances and how food will be protected if power is interrupted. The contract should state the cleanup frequency, debris removal method, working hours, and repair responsibility for scratches or damage. Take dated photos of adjacent floors, walls, counters, and furniture before work starts. Require the contractor to report water leaks, gas concerns, unsecured doors, or accidental damage immediately. A clean, controlled site reduces health, safety, and schedule problems.
acceptedAnswer.description: A contractor should isolate the work zone with zipper barriers or temporary walls, protect floors and nearby rooms, use dust extraction, seal HVAC openings when appropriate, maintain a safe path, and remove debris regularly. Confirm daily cleanup, pet and child access rules, appliance shutdowns, and emergency contact procedures before demolition.
